home.title: From super individual to super team.
home.tagline: From super individual to super team: DSH Teamwork turns DeepSeek Harness into your team's agent workspace.
home.eyebrow: The team edition of DeepSeek Harness
home.lede: DSH makes one person as productive as a small team. DSH Teamwork puts the whole team on it: shared presets, plugins and a team assistant, one budget everyone works within, and every day's work settling into skills the team keeps.
home.hint: Already on DSH? Type /teamwork login in your terminal.

shift.label: Surface · one person's work
shift.title: One person with agents goes far. A team with them goes further.
shift.lede: Every member already has an agent that writes, reviews and ships. What they lack is each other's best setup, a shared budget, and a place where good work stays.
shift.from1: Everyone tunes their own prompts and tools.
shift.to1: The best setup is published once, and everyone runs the same one.
shift.from2: API keys pasted into a chat and rotated when someone leaves.
shift.to2: Keys stay on the server; removing someone takes effect on their next request.
shift.from3: Nobody knows what the agents cost until the bill arrives.
shift.to3: Team and member budgets, with every call counted.
shift.from4: A great workflow lives and dies on one laptop.
shift.to4: It becomes the team's: versioned, reviewed and kept.

everywhere.label: Everywhere · where the work happens
everywhere.title: The same team, in every place you work.
everywhere.lede: Teamwork does not replace DSH; it follows it. The team's setup reaches the terminal, the browser and the phone, and next, agents that run in the cloud.
everywhere.terminalBody: Sign in once with /teamwork login. Team models, presets and plugins sync by themselves, next to your own setup.
everywhere.consoleBody: Admins connect models, publish presets and plugins, review what members share, and set budgets.
everywhere.mobileBody: Drive the DSH on your own computer from your phone: start a session with a team preset, follow it, answer its approvals. End-to-end encrypted.
everywhere.cloudBody: Cloud sessions and team bots on the team's own cloud computers, started from the web, the app or your DSH.

collaborate.label: Collaborate · what the team shares
collaborate.title: One person's best setup becomes everyone's.
collaborate.lede: Presets, plugins and the team assistant are published once. Every member's next sync carries them, and nothing of their own is overwritten.
collaborate.presetsBody: A role the team shares: the model it calls, the tools it needs and the way it works. Start from a template, then make it the team's.
collaborate.pluginsBody: npm packages pinned at exact versions, or the team's private packages checked file by file, so everyone runs the same build.
collaborate.assistantBody: Every new team gets one. Ask it in DSH about the team's resources, usage, budgets and members, or what is waiting for review.
collaborate.reviewBody: Any member can submit a preset or plugin from their own DSH. An admin approves the exact contents before the team gets it.
collaborate.termSession: New session with the team's pr-review preset
collaborate.termNoKey: No provider key stored on this machine

govern.label: Govern · safe to hand over
govern.title: Give everyone agents, and keep the controls.
govern.lede: An admin decides which models the team calls, how much it may spend and who is in. The server enforces it on every call.
govern.budgetsBody: Daily and monthly caps for the team, for each member and for each provider. A call reserves its cost before it runs, so a cap is not overrun.
govern.usageBody: Every model call by member and model, priced in reference points at the rates you set, and exported as CSV. No prompt or reply is stored.
govern.keysBody: Provider keys are stored encrypted, cannot be read back, and never reach a member's computer. Team-model calls go through the gateway.
govern.membersBody: Every request re-reads the caller's membership. Remove someone, and their next request is refused.
govern.promise: Nothing a caller sends can name a URL, a header or a key.
govern.promiseNote: The model is resolved within your team; the provider and its key are the server's to choose.

assets.label: Deep · what the team keeps
assets.title: Daily work settles into the team's assets.
assets.lede: A preset someone wrote on Tuesday is how the whole team works by Friday. Each publication is kept as a layer: who wrote it, who approved it, and exactly what it was.
assets.caption: An example of a team's published resources, newest on top.
assets.versionsBody: Each approved preset and plugin is a version with its author and reviewer. Compare any version with what is live today.
assets.restoreBody: An older version comes back as a draft and goes through the same review, even after the resource was deleted.
assets.exportBody: Export a resource with what it depends on, to keep a copy outside the server.
assets.nextBody: Next, what members do with their agents stays with the team too: sessions, workspaces and a memory the team can search.

community.label: Open core · run it your way
community.title: Use the hosted service, or run it on your own server.
community.lede: What one team needs is open source. What a company needs to run agents across many teams comes with the hosted service.
community.hostedBody: Nothing to install: sign in, create a team and invite people. It adds hosted models paid in advance, the mobile app and, next, DSH in the cloud.
community.openBody: Apache-2.0: teams, models, presets, plugins, the assistant, review and history, usage and budgets, and the gateway. One program from npx, a download or compose.yaml, on SQLite, Postgres or MySQL.

faq.label: Questions
faq.title: Before you start
faq.q1: Where do the provider keys live?
faq.a1: On the DSH Teamwork server, encrypted. An admin enters a key once in the team console; it cannot be read back and never reaches a member's computer. A member's DSH holds a team token that lasts 30 days and cannot call a provider by itself.
faq.q2: Do we have to change DSH?
faq.a2: No. Install the @dsh-teamwork/dsh-teamwork plugin and run /teamwork login. The team's setup syncs by itself, next to each member's own, and overwrites nothing.
faq.a3: No. Conversations stay in each member's DSH. The server forwards team-model calls to the provider and records their token counts, never the prompt or the reply.
faq.q4: What happens when we remove a member?
faq.a4: Their next request is refused. Membership is checked on every request, so there is no waiting for a token to expire.
faq.q5: Can one person be in several teams?
faq.a5: Yes. Each team checks membership on its own, and the plugin syncs every team the person is in.
faq.q6: What happens when a budget runs out?
faq.a6: A call reserves its largest possible cost before it runs, and one that would go over the cap is refused. Hard limits cover DeepSeek models called directly today; calls to other providers are counted and reported against the budget.

writer.name: Writer
writer.persona: Has written many proposals, weekly reports, official notices and articles, and turns scattered notes into text a reader takes in at a glance.
writer.description: Sets structure and tone for the reader and the occasion, outlines first, then delivers a document ready to use.
writer.deliverable: A finished draft, written to a file, with the facts you need to confirm listed at the end
writer.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's writer. You have written many proposals, weekly reports, official notices and articles, and you turn scattered notes into clear text a reader takes in at a glance.

## Method
1. First settle three things: who reads it, what they should do after reading, and how long it is. When something is missing, ask; do not guess.
2. Give an outline first, and write the draft once it is agreed.
3. Put the conclusion first; one point per paragraph; use the reader's words, not jargon.
4. Use only the numbers, dates and names in the material, and mark any without a source.

## Deliverable
The draft, written to a file, with the facts the user needs to confirm listed at the end.

analyst.name: Data analyst
analyst.persona: Knows Python (pandas) and the usual business metrics, and agrees on definitions before computing anything.
analyst.description: Reads tables, cleans them, computes metrics and charts, and gives conclusions with their definitions and a script you can rerun.
analyst.deliverable: A summary of findings, chart files, the metric definitions and a script you can rerun
analyst.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's data analyst. You know Python (pandas) and the usual business metrics, and you agree on definitions before computing anything.

## Method
1. Look at the data first: rows, columns, missing and odd values. Report them to the user.
2. Agree on each metric's definition with the user: the time range, how duplicates count, what the denominator is.
3. Compute every number with a script, never in your head, and keep the script so the result can be rerun.
4. Lead with the conclusion, each backed by a number and a chart; do not present a correlation as a cause.

## Deliverable
A summary, charts (PNG), the definitions used, and a script that reruns the analysis.

researcher.name: Research analyst
researcher.persona: Has done competitor analysis, industry research and vendor selection, and accepts only facts with a source.
researcher.description: Breaks the question down, searches and reads primary sources, and delivers a sourced comparison with a clear recommendation.
researcher.deliverable: A one-page conclusion, a comparison table and a dated list of sources
researcher.systemPrompt:
## Persona
You are the team's research analyst. You have done competitor analysis, industry research and vendor selection, and you accept only facts you can source.

## Method
1. Break the question into 3 to 5 sub-questions and agree the scope with the user.
2. Prefer primary sources: official sites, filings, documentation. Cross-check anything second-hand.
3. Give every fact its link and date; when something cannot be found, say so.
4. In a comparison, state what each option costs, and end with one clear recommendation.

## Deliverable
A one-page conclusion, a comparison table and the list of sources.
